notes: North Dakota taxable income starts from federal taxable income (Form ND-1 line 1b; line 18 subtracts line 17 from line 4b). PDF p.4: 'The starting point for computing North Dakota taxable income perpetually conforms to the computation of federal taxable income.' The federal standard deduction is therefore already inside the starting figure. Form ND-1 line 1a asks for federal AGI, but the tax is not computed from it.

The booklet prints no North Dakota standard deduction, personal exemption, dependent exemption, age-65 amount or blindness amount. base.deductions holds only the three 'other' deductions it does print.
Line 1b (PDF p.13): a federal taxable income below zero is entered as the negative number, not 0; line 18 is floored at 0.

Brackets: the schedules (PDF p.29) are headed for North Dakota taxable income of 100,000 or more; below that the Tax Table (PDF pp.22-28) applies, in 50-dollar rows rounded to whole dollars. Spot checks at the row midpoint agree with the schedule: 48,500-48,550 single 1; 81,000-81,050 joint 1; 40,500-40,550 separate 1; 65,000-65,050 head of household 1; 99,950-100,000 single 1,004, joint 371, separate 1,160, head of household 683. Qualifying surviving spouse uses the joint schedule (PDF p.29 heading).

Misprint corrected: PDF p.29, joint schedule, second row prints 'amount over $ 80.975' with a period. The rendered PDF page shows the period, so it is in the booklet itself and not a conversion error. 80,975 is used: the same page prints 80,975 in the Over and But Not Over columns; 4,233.45 = 1.95% of (298,075 - 80,975) exactly; the Tax Table first shows joint tax of 1 in the row 81,000-81,050.

Marriage penalty credit (line 22; PDF p.16 worksheet, PDF p.17 qualified income): recorded as a relief. Rendered PDF p.16 shows 15,750.00 preprinted on worksheet line 5 and 312.00 on line 13, Maximum credit. The worksheet's result is a difference of schedule taxes, which no schema field can compute, so the formula is in cap_rule.

Worked from the printed figures, not printed themselves: worksheet line 12 first turns positive when the lower qualified income passes 48,250 (for joint income in the 1.95% band), above the printed 47,550 gate, which fits the booklet's warning that meeting the conditions 'may not produce a credit'. Where both single computations and the joint computation are all in the 1.95% band the result is 311.51, so the 312 maximum binds only at higher incomes.

Pensions from other states' governments: not found in the booklet. No line, worksheet or sentence names them. A New York State pension is not mentioned; New York appears nowhere in the sources. With no subtraction line it stays in federal taxable income (line 1b). Only the peace officer exclusion could reach one, and the booklet does not settle that (covers_unclear).

North Dakota's own and federal government pensions, private pensions, IRA distributions, employer-plan distributions and annuities: no general subtraction or exemption is printed. The booklet does not say in so many words that they are taxed; they are part of federal taxable income and no line removes them. The only retirement subtractions printed are lines 8 (railroad), 9 (peace officer), 14 (military) and 15 (Social Security).
Roth conversions: not found in the booklet. No rule mentions conversions.

Lump-sum distributions are an addition: Schedule ND-1SA line 1 adds back the amount from federal Form 4972, line 6 plus line 10, for a distribution from a qualified retirement plan elected onto that form, unless received while a nonresident (Schedule ND-1SA PDF p.2).

Peace officer exclusion (line 9, PDF p.14): recorded as public_pension on the reading that a peace officer's employer plan is a government plan; both readers read it so and the booklet does not say it outright. No cap or age is printed. Years of service in other states count toward the 20, but the booklet does not say a plan of another state qualifies.

Military retirement exclusion (line 14, PDF pp.4 and 15): no cap or age printed. Federal civil service benefits as a dual status military technician qualify under the same line and stay in this entry as a condition, because they share its rule.

Railroad line 8 (PDF p.14) also takes taxable unemployment and sick pay from the Railroad Retirement Board. Taxable Tier 1 benefits go on line 8, not line 15; a filer with both splits Form 1040 line 6b by gross benefits (PDF p.15).

Military pay exclusion (line 11, PDF p.15) is recorded with covers wages because the schema has no military pay kind. Line 10 (Servicemember Civil Relief Act adjustment) is for nonresidents and is not recorded.

Municipal bond interest: the booklet prints no rule. Line 5 subtracts only U.S. obligation interest and interest exempted from state tax by federal statute. The additions on Form ND-1 lines 2-3 and Schedule ND-1SA lines 1-2 include no municipal interest. Recorded not_stated.

Not recorded as entries, no field or no figure: credit for income tax paid to another state (line 21, Schedule ND-1CR, not in the sources); other credits (line 23, Schedule ND-1TC, not in the sources); planned gift or endowment adjustment (line 2); S corporation adjustments, renaissance zone, new or expanding business, workforce recruitment and college expense reimbursement (Schedule ND-1SA); farm income averaging (Schedule ND-1FA); sale of a research credit (Schedule ND-1CS).
Reciprocity (PDF p.8) with Minnesota and Montana covers compensation for services and wages only; it says nothing about pensions.
Organ donor deduction is recorded per return and the stillborn child deduction per dependent as judgement calls; Schedule ND-1SA says neither outright.
Indexing: the booklet says nothing about inflation adjustment of any figure.
Surtaxes and recapture: none found in the booklet.

reliefs.cap_rule: Worksheet: line 4 = the smaller qualified income; line 5 = 15,750.00 (preprinted); line 6 = line 4 - line 5; line 7 = Single schedule tax on line 6; line 8 = joint taxable income (line 1) - line 6; line 9 = Single schedule tax on line 8; line 10 = joint schedule tax on line 1; line 11 = line 7 + line 9; line 12 = line 10 - line 11, and if zero or less there is no credit; line 13 Maximum credit = 312.00; line 14 = the smaller of lines 12 and 13. A filer with Schedule ND-1NR multiplies line 14 by the ratio on its line 20.
